title: Capability-gated shell execution with deny-by-default scope
problem: A general-purpose shell tool can let an agent perform actions that were never required by the task, including destructive repository or system mutations.
control: Build the executable shell capability from an explicit per-turn scope and deny commands outside that scope before process creation.
enforcement_point: The shell tool wrapper immediately before subprocess creation.

evidence.description: Synthetic examples should show an allowed read-only command succeeding and an out-of-scope destructive command being rejected before execution.

security.notes: This proposal narrows permissions. A complete implementation would also test command aliases, shell chaining, and alternate side-effecting tools.

limitations: Command classification alone does not prove semantic safety.
Equivalent side effects through other tools require separate capability gates.
